The dish is called Char Sui ribs. I believe Char Sui is Cantonese for BBQ.

It is very different from Western BBQ in the flavour and cooking ( no smoke? that's blasphemy for BBQ right?)

Here is my recipe:

2 slabs of side ribs (riblets work great) membrane removed

Marinade:

  • 1/4 cup shao xing ( Chinese cooking wine)
  • 1/4 cup Hoisin
  • 1/4 cup honey
  • 1/8 cup dark soy
  • 1/8 cup light soy
  • 2 Table spoons Siracha
  • 2 Table spoons of toasted sesame oil
  • 1 Table spoon 5 spice powder
  • 1 Table spoon garlic powder
  • 2 Table spoons onion powder
  • 2 Table spoons ginger powder

Combine all the ingredients and mix with ribs. Marinate for 1-3 days ( I prefer a three day wait but sometimes the smell can get to you and the family makes me cook earlier then I want to)

  • Set oven to 225f and place ribs on a baking rack sitting in a baking pan.
  • Put ribs in the oven and add water to the pan. ( The pan should stay wet throughout the cook)
  • Cook for 2 1/2 hours at 225f
  • At the 2.5 hour mark brush the ribs generously with honey.
  • At three hours remove ribs and brush with honey again. ( I used to brush with molasses I prefer honey now).
  • At this point try a small piece to check your salt levels, if you think it's under salted sprinkle sea salt on the tops
  • Cut up 1 bunch of green onions and garnish
  • Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds for garnish

There seem to be an awful lot of posts about what Fallout 4 did wrong and I'll admit, I've fed into that a bit myself. For some of us Fallout 4 is strange chimera, a weird juxtaposition of cool new stuff and stupid other shit we don't give a fuck about or really don't like. Unfortunately, as always, the focus is on the negative, so in an attempt to get the discussion going regarding the things Fallout 4 does right, here we go:

  • The Act of Looting: looting no longer requires you to open things up and look inside, loading an inventory exchange screen. You can loot any desk, body, chest, box, freezer, fleck of brain that used to be a raiders head, or whatever contains items without going into this screen, and you can easily see what they have inside them just by placing the crosshair over it. The list is prioritized relatively well, and I think most valuable items are at the top (you scroll through the items in the visible list with the Dpad using a controller, not sure about m/kb). BEST OF ALL , though, you can still go into that exchange screen if you want to.

  • The Loot Itself: there is finally a fucking reason to pick up ashtrays and deskfans and coffee cups and almost all the other crap just lying around the post-nuclear wasteland. This ties in to the crafting and settlement systems, so if you avoid both those systems somehow I suppose most of the loot is still pointless but if you opt to utilize either (and especially if you go for broke and utilize both) scavenging for shit in abandoned buildings and basements and wherever feels 10000x more meaningful and interesting. I actually said 'FUCK YEAH' to myself last night when I found a bunch of soap. Fucking soap. But I needed that oil...

  • Crafting Weapon and Armor Upgrades: I'm pretty sure you can't craft totally new weapons and armor like in the last 2 games but honestly, I never did that anyway; it was a pain in the ass to find the parts and then when I did the guns sucked more than the regular guns I had anyway. Skyrim's system (which is obviously the inspiration for Fallout 4s) was a bit better, but still imperfect. Fallout 4 is the first upgrade crafting system I felt really added something to the game, perhaps too much even; by character level 12 I'd taken one perk level in Armorer and one in Gunsmith, and using just the crap I had accumulated I was able to upgrade all my weapons and armor to the highest degree those perks allowed and I pretty much doubled both my damage output and damage reduction. Even 10 levels later I have the same weapons and they are still tearing through shit so it may be a little OP but regardless, I like it, and I will be taking some more perks tonight so I can properly mod out my power armor.

  • Regular Armor Complexity: holy shit Bethesda made a system MORE complicated??? Unreal. Instead of just equipping a helmet and 'armor' like previous Fallouts (1 and 2 don't even have helmets, it's just armor) this time you can equip a chest piece, right arm, left arm, right leg, left leg and helmet (and glasses and a ring), and you can wear some outfits underneath (like the Vault Suit). Considering the steady simplification of Bethesda games over the years this is a bright beacon of hope.

  • Power Armor Feels Powerful: And speaking of power armor... For those that somehow don't know, power armor runs on... power now, a seemingly finite resource is consumed when you use it for anything other than standing still or fast travel. At first, I did not like this, and just stockpiled the resource. A friend told me to just wear the shit and not worry so much, and I did, and I'm glad, because the power armor is sweet as hell. The display changes color and and has effects on it, you are taller, people notice you wearing it, and of course your strength and defense increase. The resource it uses can be found in what feels like 50% of the 'dungeons' and can be bought at the not unreasonable price of 300-400 caps depending on your charisma. I'm on the fence really as to whether or not I LIKE the new fuel mechanic but I DO like how the power armor feels, how it looks, how it can be upgraded and pieces added and removed.

  • Monster Design and Animation: The first enemy I encountered after the radroaches were molerats. Molerats have always been a Fallout staple and, despite being gross as fuck, they have always been kind of a joke. When 5 of them popped out of the ground like missiles and swarmed me I was more than a little surprised and even concerned. They looked good, moved good, and died good. I've had the same experience with nearly every monster I've encountered in the game except maybe Bloatflies which still kinda suck. The animations on the ghouls and radscorpions in particular impresses me, as does my ability to blow parts off enemies (arms and legs off ghouls, eyestalks off Mr Gutsy, etc). The graphical upgrade might not be overwhelming but it sure does look a lot better than Fallout 3 or Skyrim.

  • Legendary Stuff: Legendary enemies are a nice random challenge and legendary items are a nice random reward. I'm not 100% sure on how either are generated but I know that when I gunned down a Legendary Radroach and found a Legendary Walking Stick that did extra damage to Super Mutants, I had a smile on my face.

  • Settlements: I'm not sure I like the system overall or not, but I'm working with it and I like having shit to do. What I DEFINITELY liked, however, was being able to build a bed and a bunch of storage boxes right next to the Fast Travel point. And also being able to move the Fast Travel point. Wow. Such a small thing but it is so very nice.

  • General Graphics/Aesthetics: I like them. It's a personal taste thing but I like the 50's scifi styling everywhere. The graphics quality is good enough for me, but I play Dwarf Fortress and weird shit like Capsule so ignore me.

  • Music: The music is good. Nuff said.

  • The Vault Boy Animations: They are also good and manage to retain the old style.

EDIT1: Forgot some stuff, added below this line ____________________________

  • Justification for Not Sucking: I'm not gonna spoil anything if I can help it (I went into the game COMPLETELY BLIND, I knew 2 things: the graphics were more colorful and it looked like power armor could fly, absolutely nothing about the plot or even the intro), but the game gives you a pretty damned good justification for not needing to learn how to fire a rifle, or how to use a computer, or stimpack, or anything else. I still miss skills and feel that it would have been nice to start everything at, say, 75% and let you go to 200% but if you're going to take them away, this was the way to do it, just consider everything is at 100%. That the game story supports this is a surprising nod to consistency.

  • The Gunplay is Pretty OK: Trying to hit shit outside of VATS in FO3 or NV was like trying to unlock your door when you're drunk, you're trying to line shit up but everything is working against you. Now I can actually hit things outside of VATS, and that is pretty cool because FO3/NV really made me question my FPS skills in a bad way. I'm not saying the new gunplay is amazing or anything, but staying out of VATS feels like an option now. Part of the reason, for me at least, is that there seems to be a lot more ammo than there used to be. Also, you are skilled with all weapons right off the bat. Anyway, I like that I can sometimes go through a whole shopping center without going into VATS... except to check for ghouls playing dead like the scumbag I am.

  • On Demand Critical: If you use VATS, though, you get something pretty amazing: a little bar that charges up every time you successfully hit something in VATS, and when that bar is filled you can initiate a Critical Hit with no miss chance. Awesome. It's only one (unless you take a park) so it's not OP out of the box, but if you're hiding and see something you probably shouldn't try to take on, well, at least you have a chance. Critical hit with my sniper rifle and 2x for being Hidden is something like 220 damage, I dunno, it kills the shit out of Radstags.
